papers.title: Polar Geometry of Time-Odd EEG Dynamics
papers.summary: The paper introduces a skew-symmetric operator derived from local state derivatives and its polar decomposition to isolate time-odd EEG structure for cross-session subject matching. Across four longitudinal EEG datasets, polar orientation improved discriminability (e.g., Dortmund AUC from 0.8901 to 0.9625 and CMC@1 from 0.4757 to 0.6214), and fixed alpha-beta fusion further increased CMC@1 to 0.8350 and AUC to 0.9855.

papers.title: Chronotype-specific associations of sleep-wake schedule with behavioral, physiological, and psychological parameters.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: Compared early and late chronotypes under socially imposed versus self-selected 8-hour sleep schedules, measuring subjective states, sleep pressure via EEG, and motor and cognitive performance at 1.5 and 12.5 hours after awakening. Early chronotypes showed typical sleep pressure accumulation, late chronotypes were more affected by sleep timing, and cognitive peaks depended on chronotype and wake duration rather than clock time alone.

papers.title: Active Bed Microclimate Regulation Modulates Sleep Architecture, Autonomic, and Central Nervous System Activity during Sleep
papers.summary: Used a smart bed with six active temperature settings to test effects on sleep architecture, autonomic activity, and EEG in 18 adults across two overnight polysomnography sessions. Active cooling and heating increased slow-wave sleep odds (OR 1.21-3.65) and altered heart rate and cortical activity, suggesting nonlinear thermal effects and individualized temperature strategies.

papers.title: HIPPOCAMPAL TAU RELATED SIGNAL INDEXES HYPEREXCITABILITY AND NREM SLEEP MEMORY DYSFUNCTION IN TEMPORAL LOBE EPILEPSY
papers.summary: In 25 patients with unilateral temporal lobe epilepsy, higher ipsilateral hippocampal 18F-MK6240 tau tracer uptake was associated with greater focal seizure burden, lower N2 sleep spindle rate, higher N3 slow-wave rate, and impaired memory performance. The findings suggest hippocampal tau signal as a candidate marker of circuit vulnerability linked to NREM sleep-memory dysfunction.

papers.title: Sleep Reorganization and Sustained Attention Following Group Nap Cessation in Japanese Preschoolers.
papers.summary: This naturalistic pre-post study examined sleep reorganization and sustained attention after group nap cessation in 19 Japanese preschoolers, using wrist actigraphy and a continuous performance test. Nap cessation increased nighttime sleep by 31.6 min but reduced total sleep time by 37.2 min; greater increases in nighttime sleep were associated with fewer miss errors on the attention task at the individual level, though group-level attention changes were not significant.

papers.title: Comparison of Actigraphy and Polysomnography in a Sleep Centre Cohort.
papers.summary: This study compared MotionWatch 8 actigraphy with polysomnography in 107 sleep centre patients over eight nights. Actigraphy overestimated total sleep time by 27.31 min and sleep efficiency by 6.09%, with wide 95% limits of agreement and effects modified by older age and periodic limb movements, indicating the methods are not interchangeable.

papers.title: Altered EEG patterns co-vary with specific improvements in mind health at summer camp
papers.summary: In 30 adolescents, a three-week device-free nature-rich summer camp was followed by steeper aperiodic EEG slopes, increased DFA scaling exponents, reduced entropy and Lempel-Ziv complexity, and decreased alpha and beta power. These convergent EEG changes co-varied with improved focus, sleep quality, reduced restlessness/hyperactivity, and overall mind health, with high specificity in precision analyses.

papers.title: Are there distinctive EEG Signatures of tinnitus-related emotional distress? Evidence from spectral parameterization and source-level functional connectivity.
papers.summary: The study used resting-state EEG spectral parameterization and source-level phase-locking values to characterize oscillatory and connectivity signatures in tinnitus patients versus healthy controls. Tinnitus was associated with a higher aperiodic exponent, reduced alpha peak frequency in temporal regions, increased auditory-parietal synchronization, and decreased connectivity involving auditory, anterior cingulate, and prefrontal regions.

papers.title: IMU50: a high-frequency multi-modal wrist-worn IMU dataset of 50 subjects over 5 continuous days for supervised and self-supervised learning in free-living conditions.
papers.summary: The paper presents IMU50, a dataset of continuous wrist-worn IMU, PPG, and skin temperature recordings from 50 healthy volunteers over five consecutive days, with metabolic and clinical metadata. The dataset provides about 136 hours per subject and is intended for supervised and self-supervised learning in free-living conditions.

papers.title: Target-Session early stopping for cross-session EEG mental workload classification: a reusable deployment-oriented method.
papers.summary: Introduces Target-Session Early Stopping (TSES), which replaces the within-session validation set used for early stopping with 50 labelled epochs from the target session to improve cross-session EEG mental workload classification. TSES improved binary cross-session accuracy on all 14 directional transfer pairs across three EEG subsets and, with a Kolmogorov-Smirnov drift screen, requires about four minutes of target-session recording.

papers.title: Zwitterionic Polymer Coating Enabled Chronic Dopamine Sensing and Electrophysiology Recording in Free-Moving Mice.
papers.summary: Develops zwitterionic poly(sulfobetaine methacrylate) (PSB) coatings for Ag/AgCl reference and multimodal microelectrode arrays to enable chronic dopamine sensing and electrophysiology in freely moving mice. The PSB coating reduced protein fouling and inflammation while the hydrogel protected Ag/AgCl from delamination, yielding stable dopamine detection and electrophysiological recordings over four weeks.

papers.title: Differentially Private EEG Feature Anonymization: A Privacy-Utility Case Study in Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: The paper studies subject-level differential privacy for clinical EEG-derived feature representations using Gaussian and Laplace perturbations across client-side, server-side, and decentralized training scenarios. Results show that perturbation can be integrated into EEG workflows, but mechanism choice, privacy parameters, and sensitivity calibration strongly affect data utility, highlighting a privacy-utility trade-off in small and imbalanced clinical EEG datasets.

papers.title: Oxygen, carbon dioxide, and nitric oxide: role in the pathophysiology of obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: A narrative review of how oxygen, carbon dioxide, and nitric oxide contribute to obstructive sleep apnea pathophysiology. It describes chronic intermittent hypoxia activating HIF-1alpha and NF-kappaB pathways, intermittent hypercapnia affecting chemoreflex and autonomic function, and reduced nitric oxide bioavailability, linking these to cardiovascular, metabolic, and neurocognitive risks.

papers.title: Insulin Dosing Is Associated With Cardiac Sympathetic Predominance Independent of Glycemic Profiles in Type 1 Diabetes Under Free-Living Conditions.
papers.summary: Examines whether insulin dosing is associated with cardiac autonomic balance in adults with type 1 diabetes under free-living conditions. Higher last bolus and basal insulin doses were associated with increased cardiac sympathetic predominance during early and late sleep phases, respectively, independent of glycemic profiles.

papers.title: Melatonin and Artificial Light: Effects on Maternal and Fetal Health During Pregnancy.
papers.summary: Reviewed evidence on melatonin's role during pregnancy and the effects of artificial light at night (ALAN) on maternal-fetal health, synthesizing human and animal studies. Exposure to ALAN reduces melatonin production and is associated with adverse maternal-fetal outcomes, while animal studies demonstrate causal effects of melatonin disruption and protective effects of supplementation; evidence is insufficient to recommend melatonin supplementation, but circadian hygiene measures may be advised.

papers.title: Causal Effects of Gut Microbiota on Morning Chronotype, Insomnia and Sleep Duration: A Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization Study.
papers.journal: Journal of central nervous system disease
papers.summary: Conducted a two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis using genome-wide association data to infer causal effects of 196 gut microbiota taxa on morning chronotype, insomnia, and sleep duration. Identified specific taxa positively and negatively associated with sleep traits, including Bifidobacteriales/Bifidobacteriaceae/Bifidobacterium negatively with morning chronotype, Oscillibacter negatively with insomnia, and Lentisphaerae/Victivallaceae positively with sleep duration.

papers.title: High Adhesion Superoleophobic Oil Microdroplets to Create Ocular Hypertension In Vivo.
papers.summary: Introduces an injectable oil microdroplet model that creates sustained ocular hypertension in mice, producing a 44.3% loss of retinal ganglion cells within four weeks via a self-locking mechanism in trabecular architecture. The model also showed increased nocturnal sleepiness, mirroring daytime sleepiness in human glaucoma patients.

papers.title: The association of sleep health with epigenetic aging in early adolescence: exploratory insights from the Health Outcomes and Measures of the Environment study.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: This exploratory study examined associations between accelerometry-based sleep characteristics and epigenetic aging in 138 adolescents from the HOME Study. Overall associations were imprecise, but higher sleep fragmentation was associated with elevated epigenetic age acceleration among males (Hannum β = 0.885, 95% CI: 0.132, 1.638; interaction p = .005) but not females.

papers.title: Sex and stress paradigm influence behavioural, neuroimmune, and microbiome responses in pubertal CD-1 mice.
papers.summary: This study compared chronic unpredictable stress (14 or 28 days) and 7-day sleep disruption in pubertal male and female CD-1 mice, measuring behaviour, plasma cytokines, prefrontal cortex and hippocampal inflammasome gene expression, and gut microbiome composition. It found stressor- and sex-specific effects, with sleep disruption producing the strongest behavioural and gut-immune alterations, including reduced short-chain fatty acid-producing taxa and increased stress-associated genera.

papers.title: Longitudinal Study on Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder, Anxiety, and Depression Among Medical Staff in China.
papers.summary: This longitudinal study followed 2,650 Chinese medical staff over two time points six months apart to examine anxiety, depression, and PTSD prevalence and bidirectional predictive relationships. It found that prevalence of all three conditions increased from T1 to T2, and cross-lagged models showed PTSD predicted later anxiety and depression, while depression predicted later PTSD and anxiety, but anxiety did not predict depression or PTSD.

papers.title: Smartphone Addiction as a Predictor of Poor Sleep Quality Among Secondary School Students: A School-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed 400 secondary school students in Upper Egypt to assess smartphone addiction severity and sleep quality using the SAS-SV and PSQI. It found that 50% reported moderate smartphone addiction and 65% had poor sleep quality, with smartphone addiction positively correlated with poorer sleep quality and more than five-fold increased odds of poor sleep quality after adjustment.

papers.title: Effect of fezolinetant on sleep, health-related quality of life and work productivity.
papers.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
papers.summary: This post-hoc analysis of pooled SKYLIGHT 1 and 2 trial data evaluated fezolinetant's impact on sleep disturbance and impairment in women with moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause. It found that fezolinetant 30 mg and 45 mg improved sleep disturbance and impairment versus placebo at 12 weeks, with benefits maintained over 1 year, and improvements in VMS and sleep were associated with better work productivity.

papers.title: The BIG-5 of pain, anxiety, stress, sleep disturbances, and delirium, and the effects of music in hospitalized patients.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the occurrence and consequences of pain, anxiety, stress, sleep disturbances, and delirium (the BIG-5) in hospitalized surgical patients, and summarizes findings on music intervention as a complementary therapy. It concludes that music intervention effectively reduces each component of the BIG-5 and decreases analgesic requirements, supporting its implementation in routine perioperative care.

papers.title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing and Nocturnal Hypoxia in Cancer Patients: A Stomatological and Airway Assessment Framework.
papers.summary: This narrative review proposes a stomatological and upper airway assessment framework to identify anatomical contributors to sleep-disordered breathing and nocturnal hypoxia in adults with cancer. It highlights that features such as maxillary constriction, nasal airway narrowing, altered craniofacial development, and ankyloglossia may contribute to upper airway dysfunction yet are rarely incorporated into routine oncological assessment.

papers.title: Self-Reported Sleep Duration After Kidney Transplantation Requires Medication-Aware Interpretation.
papers.summary: This letter argues that self-reported sleep duration after kidney transplantation requires medication-aware interpretation, likely emphasizing the impact of immunosuppressive regimens on sleep. No abstract is provided, so specific findings cannot be summarized.

papers.title: Weight Reduction Heterogenicity and Mediators of GLP-1RAs and Dual Agonists for Individuals With Obesity: A Meta-Analysis.
papers.summary: This meta-regression of 32 trials (40,408 participants) found that GLP-1RAs and dual agonists achieved a pooled mean weight reduction of 9.36% with high heterogeneity. Tirzepatide and treatment duration ≥72 weeks were associated with greater weight loss, while baseline anxiety/depression positively predicted efficacy and comorbid T2DM, OSA, and MAFLD negatively correlated with response.

papers.title: The Relationship of Postearthquake Trauma With Risk Perception and Substance Use in Southeast Turkey.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study in earthquake-affected southeastern Turkey examined associations between postearthquake trauma, risk perception, and substance use. It reported that substance use due to sadness/distress was linked to higher emotional risk perception and post-traumatic stress symptoms, and amphetamine users had higher post-traumatic stress than marijuana users; increased post-earthquake substance use was associated with excitement restriction and sleep disturbance.

papers.title: Health-related factors and their impact on blood-based biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: This CSF-confirmed cohort study (n=116) tested associations between modifiable health-related factors and plasma biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease. Age was the most consistent predictor of plasma NFL and pTau181, and APOE ε3/ε4 was associated with higher pTau181, while metabolic and lifestyle factors showed only weak or inconsistent associations.

papers.title: Association Between Sleep Duration and Depressive Symptoms Among U.S. Adults: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2021-2023.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional NHANES 2021–2023 analysis of 3,727 U.S. adults found that short sleep duration was associated with higher odds of clinically significant depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 ≥10), with the strongest association among those sleeping ≤5 hours (aOR 3.21, 95% CI 2.18–4.75) compared to 7–8 hours.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence at the Boundary of Spiritual Experience and Psychopathology: A Scoping Review of Evidence from Türkiye, the USA, the UK, Poland, South Korea, and Israel.
papers.summary: A scoping review of nine studies from six countries mapped how AI mediates, reinforces, detects, predicts, or interprets religious and spiritual experiences at the boundary with psychosis and dissociation. Conversational AI was reported as a catalyst, amplifier, co-author, or object of spiritually framed delusions, while NLP and machine-learning models showed preliminary potential for identifying psychotic episodes and predicting relapse.

papers.title: From HIV to SARS-CoV-2 associated neurological disorder ("HAND" to "SAND"): Viral infection as a "time-bomb" for the aging brain.
papers.summary: This review proposes the term SARS-CoV-2 Associated Neurological Disorder (SAND) by analogy to HIV-associated neurological disorder (HAND), arguing that SARS-CoV-2 infection, like HIV, may act as a time-bomb for the aging brain. It reports that Long Covid cognitive symptoms mirror HAND and that viral proteins, neuroinflammation, barrier disruption, and mitochondrial decline may accelerate Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease risk without substantial evidence of direct brain infection.

papers.title: Marfan-Like Clinical Features in DLG4 (Discs Large MAGUK Scaffold Protein 4)-Related Synaptopathy: A Brazilian Case Report.
authors: Anna Carolina De Rizzo Cantoni Rosa
papers.summary: This case report describes a 21-year-old Brazilian man with DLG4-related synaptopathy presenting with chronic pain, sensory hypersensitivity, tremors, cognitive decline, autism spectrum traits, psychotic manifestations, and marfanoid features. Whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous DLG4 missense variant of uncertain significance (c.149A>T; p.Tyr50Phe), broadening the possible phenotypic spectrum but limiting definitive genotype-phenotype correlation.

papers.title: Effects of multiple object tracking training on visual attention and sports decision-making in novice female basketball players: evidence from EyeLink-EEG synchronization.
papers.summary: This study tested whether nine weeks of multiple-object tracking (MOT) training improves sports decision-making in 56 novice female basketball players using synchronized EyeLink eye-tracking and EEG. The intervention group showed significantly improved decision accuracy, increased fixation on key areas, simplified visual search, and altered ERP components (decreased N1, P1, and LPC; increased LNC), indicating more efficient cognitive resource allocation.

papers.title: Pediatric Epiglottopexy: A Scoping Review of Indications, Techniques, Outcomes, and Complications.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-ScR scoping review mapped 24 studies (371 pediatric patients) on epiglottopexy for laryngomalacia, epiglottic prolapse, and obstructive sleep apnea. It reports consistently improved respiratory outcomes, largely preserved or improved swallowing, low complication and recurrence rates, and expanded indications from drug-induced sleep endoscopy, while noting limited evidence from small retrospective series.

papers.title: Perceived Importance of the Lifestyle Medicine Pillars on Wellbeing Among U.S. Adults: Prevalence and Sociodemographic Correlates.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional analysis of nationally representative Pew Research Center data (n=10,133 U.S. adults) examined perceived importance of lifestyle medicine pillars for wellbeing. Sleep (82.0%), stress management (79.9%), and healthy eating (69.6%) were rated highly important, while community involvement (21.8%) was lowest; younger age and lower education were associated with lower valuation of several pillars, and women valued most behaviors more highly.

papers.title: Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Peripheral Neuropathic Pain: From Cortical Analgesia to Phenotype-Stratified Clinical Translation.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes randomized trials, systematic reviews, consensus guidance, and mechanistic studies on repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for peripheral neuropathic pain, reporting that high-frequency M1 stimulation has the most defensible clinical signal. A cited 2026 meta-analysis of nine sham-controlled trials and 435 patients found reduced pain intensity after rTMS (SMD, -1.11; 95% CI, -1.72 to -0.49), with the most consistent phenotype-specific evidence in postherpetic neuralgia, and the authors propose an aetiology-stratified translational framework.

papers.title: Orofacial pain and dysfunction: From a TMD-centered discipline to a network of interconnected conditions.
papers.summary: This letter argues that the field of Orofacial Pain and Dysfunction has evolved from a temporomandibular disorder-centered discipline into a network of interconnected conditions with biopsychosocial underpinnings and links to headache, bruxism, sleep disorders, and systemic health. It emphasizes the need for interdisciplinary collaboration and integration of dental and medical expertise in education, research, and patient care.

papers.title: Mapping the Symptom Networks of Depression, Anxiety, and Their Comorbidity Among Chinese Individuals Under Community Correction.
papers.summary: This study used network analysis of SAS and SDS responses from 818 Chinese individuals under community correction to map symptom networks of anxiety, depression, and comorbidity, finding that 36.7% reported depression, 13.1% anxiety, and 11.0% comorbidity. 'Panic' was central in the anxiety network, 'emptiness' central in depression, 'fatigue' was a key trigger in the comorbidity DAG, and 'insomnia' and 'sleep disturbance' were bridge symptoms.

papers.title: Innovative mHealth Intervention Providing Sustained Anticipatory Guidance (Zero Cavity): Design, Validation, User Perception and Effectiveness - A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol
papers.summary: This protocol describes a two-arm parallel randomized controlled trial that will enroll 540 mother-infant dyads in Chennai, India to evaluate the 'Zero Cavity' mHealth app delivering sustained anticipatory guidance for early childhood caries prevention versus standard care. The primary outcome is app effectiveness in preventing ECC, with secondary outcomes including ECC incidence and prevalence, using ICDAS II criteria and semi-annual data collection.

papers.title: Clinical efficacy of an extended local treatment in nasal polyps with different endotypes: A prospective randomized controlled study.
papers.summary: This prospective randomized controlled trial in 138 patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps compared three two-week corticosteroid delivery methods and assessed whether extending treatment duration improves outcomes. Adding intranasal drops to nasal spray improved VAS and SNOT-22 extranasal and sleep symptoms compared with spray alone, while oral prednisone reduced polyp size more effectively, especially in type-2 CRSwNP.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
